en: Taal Volcano features a unique nested structure with Volcano Island situated inside Lake Taal, which itself sits within a larger volcanic caldera.
Palawan is the oldest landmass in the Philippines, forming a land bridge to Borneo during the Ice Age when sea levels were much lower.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching over 500 kilometers through the Cagayan Valley before emptying into the Babuyan Channel.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest peak in the Philippines at 2,954 meters, hosting the rare and endemic Philippine eagle within its lush forests.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, formed by volcanic activity and tectonic shifts, covering an area of over 900 square kilometers.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River features an eight-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the sea, making it uniquely subject to ocean tidal influences.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 perfectly cone-shaped limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season, resembling giant chocolate kisses.
The Philippine Trench contains the Galathea Depth, the deepest point in the Philippine Sea, plunging over 10,540 meters below the ocean's surface.
The Banaue Rice Terraces reach elevations of up to 1,500 meters above sea level, creating a massive ancient irrigation system carved entirely by hand.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is a pristine coral atoll in the Sulu Sea that houses over 600 fish species and 360 distinct coral species.
Mayon Volcano in Albay features a perfectly symmetrical natural cone, which was formed by centuries of precisely layered lava flows and volcanic ash deposits.
The Verde Island Passage between Batangas and Mindoro is the center of marine shorefish biodiversity, boasting the highest fish species density on Earth.
